items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Then we would Baron, what was his name, he was another leader up there that had a band, and you used to free lance up there with different conductors.

ctx.x: Billy Taylor and George Johnson, saxophone, four of us. Well there's where you gained an awful lot of experience, there with Raymond, because we were doing the Perry Como show at that time, he was doing a sustaining program, three to 3:15 in the afternoon, Perry Como, then Dorothy Collins. Then we would Baron, what was his name, he was another leader up there that had a band, and you used to free lance up there with different conductors. Play all different styles of music. Raymond, of course, as you know was a…

saxophone, Billy Taylor bass and me, and Raymond, we used to play the blues, Good Morning Blues program, then sometimes we'd get out of that idiom, start playing up tempo things, 'After You've Gone' and things like that. And it called for an awful lot of control, especially that time in the morning, eight o'clock in the morning you know to get those breakneck tempos.
